verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of printed page 857 (PDF p879) shows the left index column with two levels: main entries at the margin (Static data, STATUS KEY clause, STOP 387, STRONG phrase, SUB-QUEUE clause, Switch-name, SYMBOLIC QUEUE clause, System-name 71, and so on) and sub-entries indented beneath them (Declarative 382, Procedural 382, CD entry 656, TYPEDEF clause 359, Data-name 86, Condition-name 86, CORRESPONDING phrase 401, Definition 16, SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph 194/195, Figurative constant 81, Scope of 103, SET statement 517). The markdown gives every left-column line the same 3-space prefix, with no   marker, so the two levels are lost. Three leading spaces are not significant in Markdown, so the rendered page shows a flat list. The right column (System-names 194 onward) keeps the hierarchy with  . The quoted text in both sources is accurate and no words are missing. What is lost is the parent-child structure, so a reader cannot tell that 'CD entry 656' sits under STATUS KEY clause, SUB-QUEUE clause and the SYMBOLIC * clauses, or that 'TYPEDEF clause 359' sits under STRONG phrase. The page is part of the informative index, so the loss is structural and has no normative effect. The kind label 'misplaced-content' is inaccurate because nothing is moved: the content is in the right order with its indentation flattened.
verdict.corrected_description: Lost index hierarchy, not misplaced content. In the left column of the markdown (Declarative 382 through System-name 71), every line has the same 3-space indent, which Markdown ignores, so the 17 sub-entries printed indented in the PDF (Declarative 382, Procedural 382, CD entry 656 x5, TYPEDEF clause 359, Data-name 86, Condition-name 86, CORRESPONDING phrase 401, Definition 16, Condition-name 102, SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph 194/195, Figurative constant 81, Scope of 103, SET statement 517) cannot be told apart from main entries. They should carry the   prefix that the right column uses. Every word and page number is present and in order. Structural, informative index only.
